basis_note: WHAT THE NUMBER ON THE CONTRACT MEANS. `employees.ctc` is one figure and it is read by payroll every month, so whether it is a year's cost or a month's is the single most consequential fact about it — and it was nowhere. The column held annual figures (₹7,20,000) and the register used them as the month's gross, so every payslip in the product was twelve times too high, under a per-line derivation that was arithmetically perfect and therefore completely convincing. It is declared here, not assumed in code, because it differs by customer: an agency quoting monthly CTC sets `monthly` and changes no code. It sits on the effective-dated version because a company that switches its contracts over does so FROM A DATE, and payslips issued before that date must keep meaning what they meant.
note: The structure this build ships with. It is DATA: nothing below appears in a PHP file, so a new component, a changed percentage or a new statutory flag is an edit here, not a release.

components.note: is_synth_base is the wage-base flag the synthetic statutory pack asks for. A statutory scheme this build has not met yet is a FLAG SOMEBODY ADDS HERE, not a release — which is why the pack names a flag and never a list of component codes.

note: THE SAME STRUCTURE WITH A CAP ON THE HRA — the worked example of the `formula` basis, and the first component in this product that could not be expressed at all before it existed. C-HRA is still 40% of C-BASIC and it is still an earning that prorates; what is new is that it stops at ₹20,000 a month, which is the single most common thing a customer asks of an HRA and which none of `flat`, `percent_of_gross`, `percent_of`, `balance` or `schedule` can say. Nothing above changed: this is a NEW effective-dated version from the start of the 2027-28 financial year, so every payslip issued for a month before that date is computed by, and reproduces from, the version that was in force then. NOTHING HERE IS A NEW LINE — the payslip still has C-BASIC, C-HRA, C-SPECIAL and D-PT, and where the cap does not bind (a basic under ₹50,000) every figure is identical to the version above. Where it does bind, the balance component absorbs what the cap took off, so the earnings still sum to the gross exactly.

formula.description: House rent allowance is 40% of C-BASIC and stops at ₹20,000 for the month. The cap is on the month's own figure, not a twelfth of an annual one: in a part-paid month C-BASIC is already prorated, so 40% of it is the smaller number and the cap simply does not bind.
sample_cases: full month under the cap (basic ₹30,000 → HRA ₹12,000)
full month at the cap (basic ₹60,000 → HRA ₹20,000, not ₹24,000)
half a month at the capped rate (basic ₹30,000 → HRA ₹12,000, ₹8,000 less than a full month)
